producer_report.summary: Study is now selectable and has a pinned-read module. The firstmate SHA itself is NOT recorded, because this producer had no network. `athena.toml` now has `[capabilities.study]`, so the reader's catalog offers `change` and `study`, and the reader schema's capability enum is ["change","study",null]. `[capabilities.change]` is unchanged. The study verifier grant is read-only git (status, diff, log, show) plus `ls`. The study producer adds `rm` and `mv`, and no grant has a network command. The study source is recorded in `[capabilities.study.env]` as `ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_URL`, which is https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate. New `athena_cap_study::source` has `SourcePin`, which accepts only 40 lowercase hex characters, so short, abbreviated, mixed-case, branch-name or missing values are errors. `materialise` runs the git CLI itself (init, fetch of that one commit, detached checkout), checks `HEAD` equals the pin, and removes the write bits from the tree. `remove` restores write access and deletes the tree. I used the git CLI rather than a crate (buy-first); the pin is in the env table rather than a new config type, so `athena-data` is untouched. The study card, producer prompt, CHANGELOG, `docs/architecture.md` and new decision D75 (with alternatives) record the call, and say running firstmate stays out of scope. Tests use a local fixture repository, with no network.

checks_run.note: all pass, including the new source tests, the catalog test, the budgets test, and the boundary scan in xtask

open_issues: Criterion 3 is not met. `ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_SHA` (firstmate's main head) is not recorded in `athena.toml` or in CHANGELOG.md, because I had no network. Until the user adds it, `SourcePin::from_config` returns a 'no ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_SHA' error, which is the intended refusal. A follow-up edit to `athena.toml` and CHANGELOG.md is needed.
Nothing in Athena's run flow calls `materialise` yet. The module and its tests exist; wiring it into the study run step is a later job.
Only the unit tests exercise the git fetch against a local fixture. Fetching a bare SHA from github.com depends on GitHub allowing it, and I did not verify that.
mistakes: My first card and prompt additions broke the token budgets test. I shortened them, and the final run is green.
My first materialise test asserted that a write fails, which is false under root. I replaced it with a permission-bit check.
learnings: `CapabilityConfig` has `deny_unknown_fields`, so a source table needs an `athena-data` change. The `env` table takes any string, so the pin lives there.

The reader budget test counts every registered capability's card, with 1800 tokens at ceil(bytes/3). The producer set budget is 1100 tokens. Both were nearly full, so card and prompt wording had to be trimmed.
Bash in this job allows only cargo, git status/diff/log/show, ls, rm, mv and chmod. Plain `cargo ... --locked` failed after the dependency edit until one `cargo check --offline` refreshed Cargo.lock.
The tools run as root, so a write to a read-only file succeeds. The test checks the permission bits instead.
athena-cap-study may not depend on athena-git (architecture direction rule), so `source` calls git with std::process::Command.
desires: Network access (or a way to read firstmate's main head) to resolve the SHA.
A config type that allows a dedicated `[capabilities.study.source]` table.
